title: Markets: Wednesday 28 October

morning.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · before the 10:00 open
summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 7,722.6 and the Nasdaq 1.2% to 26,477.8 (snapshot), with chip stocks among the gainers, before Microsoft and Alphabet results, and ASX 200 futures pointed to a slightly higher open ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-steady-wall-street-gains-oil-slips-20261028-p61959)). Brent fell for a second session, and Iranian state media said Iran and the visiting Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials agreed to keep talking ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/oil-eases-on-middle-east-diplomacy-hopes-saudi-attacks-keep-supply-worries-alive-4974185)).

For Australia, today's September-quarter CPI is the swing factor for a 3 November hike. ASX 30-day futures priced a 60% chance at Tuesday's close, down from 62% on Monday ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). CBA, NAB and ANZ forecast a 1.0% rise in the trimmed mean and Westpac 0.9%, against the RBA's 0.8% forecast ([investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/australia-cpi-preview-banks-see-1-0-core-rise-above-the-rba-s-0-8-forecast/)).

Next: Governor Bullock's team at Senate Estimates at 11:15am, CPI at 11:30am, and an RBNZ decision at noon with a hike to 3.00% expected ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/coming-up/), [RNZ](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/business/2197473/rbnz-set-to-raise-benchmark-interest-rate-despite-previously-signalled-pause)). Then the Fed at 5am Thursday, where CME FedWatch put a hold at 90.6%, with Alphabet and Microsoft results soon after ([Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/federal-reserve-expected-hold-interest-rates-steady-midterm-elections-week-away)).

cards.headline: Chip stocks lift Wall Street before Microsoft and Alphabet report
cards.takeaway: The Nasdaq rose 1.2% as chipmakers rallied, while the Dow barely moved and Boeing reported a quarterly loss.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's issue covered Anthropic's IPO filing and Meta's capital raising. New: a second day of chip gains, Boeing's results and US orders data, with Alphabet and Microsoft now a day away.
cards.what_happened: The S&P 500 rose 0.6% and the Nasdaq 1.2% (snapshot), while the Dow added 15.99 points to 52,377.57 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-october-27-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-tech-sector-160557664.html)). The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained more than 3% ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-steady-wall-street-gains-oil-slips-20261028-p61959)). Boeing reported a third-quarter net loss of US$116 million on revenue of US$24.2 billion and a record US$745 billion backlog ([Boeing](https://investors.boeing.com/investors/news/press-release-details/2026/Boeing-Reports-Third-Quarter-Results/default.aspx)). US durable goods orders rose 1.8% in September to US$345.4 billion, after a 0.1% rise in August ([US Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/manufacturing/m3/adv/current/index.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Gains were led by technology and chip stocks. Alphabet and Microsoft report after the US close on Wednesday, which is Thursday morning Sydney time, and Amazon follows a day later ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/25/earnings-week-alphabet-microsoft-amazon.html)). LSEG data cited by CNBC show analysts expect Microsoft revenue growth of 16.8% and Alphabet of about 25%.
cards.market_reaction: The VIX fell 0.87 points to 17.52 (snapshot, delayed).
cards.what_to_watch: Alphabet and Microsoft results and capital-spending guidance, about 7am Thursday Sydney time.

competing_views.view: "Our 3Q partner checks were strong, with MSFT's net results inflecting higher and demand for prepackaged AI solutions leading the list."
Concerns about companies' AI spending sparked a sell-off last Thursday that gave the Nasdaq its worst session since June.

cards.headline: Oil falls for a second day as Iran talks continue
cards.takeaway: December Brent had its biggest one-day fall since 5 October; SEB says prices still carry a risk premium for a possible attack on Iran.
cards.key_figure: Gold futures +0.9% to US$4,073.3 · Brent: see comparison below
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's issue covered Monday's dip on the Tehran talks. New: a larger fall on Tuesday, the talks continuing, and a Houthi strike claim on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (see the Iran card).
cards.what_happened: December Brent fell 1.67%, its largest one-day fall since 5 October, though it is still up 10% month to date ([Morningstar/Dow Jones](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202610278923/front-month-ice-brent-crude-fell-167-to-settle-at-11388-data-talk)). US crude settled 1.83% lower at US$99.90 ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/oil-eases-on-middle-east-diplomacy-hopes-saudi-attacks-keep-supply-worries-alive-4974185)). Prices hit session highs after Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported missiles had targeted Ras Tanura, then fell after Iran's Supreme Leader called for proposals on conditions to end the war, according to [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/crude-wrap-wti-z6-settles-usd-186-lower-at-9990bbl).
cards.why_it_matters: Fuel is expected to be a large part of today's Australian CPI: CommBank forecasts fuel prices rose 9.8% in September, taking annual fuel inflation to about 24% ([CommBank](https://www.commbank.com.au/articles/newsroom/2026/10/inflation-cpi-rba-interest-rates-november.html)).
cards.market_reaction: Gold futures rose 0.9% to US$4,073.3 (snapshot, delayed). The snapshot's Brent futures change is not usable today; see the comparison.
cards.priced_in: SEB's Bjarne Schieldrop said prices still carry a "significant risk premium" for the risk of a US or Israeli attack on Iran ([Reuters via Euronext](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/oil-falls-2-middle-east-talks-help-ease-supply-worries)).
cards.what_to_watch: The OPEC+ meeting on Sunday (Newsquawk) and any confirmation of damage at Ras Tanura.

competing_views.view: Expects Brent to stay near US$110 a barrel through year-end, up from its previous US$100 forecast.
Prices still carry a "significant risk premium" for a possible US or Israeli attack on Iran.

comparison.title: Did Brent fall 1.7% or 5.3% on Tuesday?
comparison.why_different: Different contracts and dates. December Brent, the front month in most news reports, settled at US$113.88, down 1.67%. The snapshot's continuous series (Yahoo BZ=F) has rolled to January (US$109.68) but compares it with December's Monday settle of US$115.81, so its −5.3% is a contract-roll artefact. January's own settle was US$109.41 (Newsquawk). The FRED spot series is an EIA assessment that lags by about a week. Don't use the snapshot's −5.3%.

cards.headline: ASX set for a small gain before the CPI release
cards.takeaway: Futures pointed slightly higher after Tuesday's 0.5% rise, but CPI at 11:30am is likely to set the day's direction.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's issue previewed a flat-to-higher open. New: Tuesday's close, led by miners, and today's CPI release. Correction: Tuesday's close wrap gave the ASX 200 close as 8,852.1; the official close in the snapshot is 8,850.1.
cards.what_happened: The ASX 200 rose 0.5% to 8,850.1 on Tuesday (snapshot), led by materials as BHP and Rio Tinto gained, according to our close wrap. ASX 200 futures pointed to a slightly higher open this morning ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-steady-wall-street-gains-oil-slips-20261028-p61959), [ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-10-28/asx-markets-business-live-news/107316614)). Our data has no futures or iron ore feed today.
cards.why_it_matters: A hot CPI print would raise the odds of a hike to an 18-year-high cash rate (AFR). A soft print would lower those odds.
cards.market_reaction: The Australian dollar was at US70.21 cents at the RBA's 4pm Tuesday fix, down 0.14% on the day (snapshot); the overnight move is not in our data.
cards.what_to_watch: CPI at 11:30am and Governor Bullock's comments at Senate Estimates from 11:15am.

cards.headline: Court to rule on Star's anti-money laundering penalty today
cards.takeaway: AUSTRAC has sought A$400 million; Star says more than A$100 million payable within a year would be challenging.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Flagged as "still open" in Tuesday's close wrap. The judgment is due this morning.
cards.what_happened: Federal Court Justice Cameron Moore is due to hand down his penalty judgment in AUSTRAC's case against Star Entertainment on Wednesday morning. AUSTRAC has sought a A$400 million penalty; Star has submitted that a penalty of more than A$100 million payable within 12 months would be challenging ([SMH](https://www.smh.com.au/business/companies/judgment-day-looms-for-star-casino-as-court-decides-size-of-fine-20261026-p617g0.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: The size and timing of the penalty bear directly on Star's funding position; the judgment is a key stock-specific event on the ASX today.
cards.what_to_watch: The penalty amount and payment terms, and any Star statement to the ASX after the judgment.

competing_views.view: More than A$100 million payable within 12 months would be challenging for the company.

cards.headline: CPI today decides whether the RBA hikes next week
cards.takeaway: The big four banks expect core inflation above the RBA's forecast but are split two-two on whether that means a hike on 3 November.
cards.key_figure: RBA cash rate 4.60% · Hike odds 60% (ASX 30-day futures, Tuesday close, RBA Watch)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's issue reported 62% odds at Monday's close. New: odds eased to 60% at Tuesday's close, and the release is today.
cards.what_happened: The ABS releases September-quarter and September-month CPI at 11:30am. ASX 30-day interbank futures implied a 60% chance of a 25bp hike on 3 November at Tuesday's close (expected rate 4.75%), down from 62% on Monday ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)).
cards.why_it_matters: CBA, NAB and ANZ forecast a 1.0% quarterly rise in the trimmed mean and Westpac 0.9%, all above the RBA's August forecast of 0.8% ([investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/australia-cpi-preview-banks-see-1-0-core-rise-above-the-rba-s-0-8-forecast/)). CommBank expects annual headline inflation of 3.9%, and 4.2% over the year to September on the monthly measure, up from 4.0%, with fuel adding about 0.3 points to the monthly rise ([CommBank](https://www.commbank.com.au/articles/newsroom/2026/10/inflation-cpi-rba-interest-rates-november.html)).
cards.priced_in: A hike is more likely than not in futures pricing, so a print in line with forecasts may move markets less than a miss in either direction.
cards.what_to_watch: The quarterly trimmed mean against 1.0%, then Governor Bullock at Senate Estimates (11:15am, before the release).

competing_views.view: Expect the cash rate to stay at 4.60%.

cards.headline: Fed expected to hold on Thursday, with December still in play
cards.takeaway: Futures price a hold this week but a likely hike in December, with US inflation at 3.7%.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's issue cited 10.5% odds of a hike this week. New: FedWatch's hold probability rose to 90.6%, CNBC published its Fed Survey, and the meeting began.
cards.what_happened: The Fed began its two-day meeting on Tuesday ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-october-27-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-tech-sector-160557664.html)). CME FedWatch put a 90.6% chance on a hold at 3.75–4.00%, up from 84.5% a week earlier, and 75.1% on a 25bp hike in December ([Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/federal-reserve-expected-hold-interest-rates-steady-midterm-elections-week-away)). In CNBC's Fed Survey, 93% of respondents expect a pause and 76% a December hike, while 30% say the Fed should hike now ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/27/federal-reserve-rate-hike-timing-expectations.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: US CPI was 3.7% over the year to September (Fox Business). A December hike would narrow the gap between the US and Australian policy rates.
cards.market_reaction: The US 10-year yield fell 1bp to 4.99% and the 2-year rose 2bp to 4.70% (snapshot, Treasury par curve).
cards.what_to_watch: The statement at 5am Thursday Sydney time and Chair Warsh's press conference at 5:30am.

competing_views.view: "This isn't the time for more Fed rate hikes."

competing_views.who: Heather Long, Navy Federal Credit Union

cards.headline: US consumer confidence rebounds in October
cards.takeaway: Confidence rose far more than economists had forecast.
cards.what_happened: The Conference Board's index rose to 91.7 in October from an upwardly revised 84.2 in September. The present situation index was 120.4 and the expectations index 72.6 ([Conference Board](https://www.conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence/index.cfm)). Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 81 ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/us-consumer-confidence-improves-in-october-4976114)).
cards.why_it_matters: The Conference Board linked the rise to easing petrol prices, though consumers' write-in responses still cited rising costs (Reuters). It comes a day before the Fed decision.
cards.what_to_watch: US September-quarter GDP and core PCE on Thursday night Sydney time.

cards.headline: RBNZ expected to lift its cash rate to 3.00% at noon
cards.takeaway: A third straight hike is widely expected, ten days before New Zealand's general election.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Previewed in earlier issues. New: bank economists' latest calls; the decision is today.
cards.what_happened: The RBNZ announces at 2pm NZ time (noon Sydney), with economists expecting a 25bp rise to 3.00% despite an earlier signal of a pause ([RNZ](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/business/2197473/rbnz-set-to-raise-benchmark-interest-rate-despite-previously-signalled-pause)).
cards.why_it_matters: A hike would be the RBNZ's third in a row, with BNZ pointing to higher oil prices and a weaker currency; it lands half an hour after Australian CPI.
cards.what_to_watch: Whether the vote is split and what the RBNZ signals for December.

competing_views.view: "It would be a material shock to markets if the RBNZ did not lift the OCR."
Expects a hike today but has pencilled in a pause in December.

cards.headline: Israel's exit polls show neither bloc with a majority
cards.takeaway: Likud is the largest party, but the parties opposing Netanyahu have more seats combined; Times of Israel says coalition talks or a repeat election could follow.
cards.new_since_last_issue: New. Polls closed at 7am Sydney time.
cards.what_happened: Channel 12's exit poll put the Jewish-led opposition bloc on 52 seats, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc on 50 and Arab-led parties on 18, with 61 needed for a majority. Likud is the largest party on 24 seats, ahead of Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar on 22 ([Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/channel-12-exit-poll-shows-no-clear-victor-netanyahus-likud-is-largest-party-but-his-opponents-have-bigger-bloc/)). Another broadcaster's poll had Likud on 25. Turnout was 74.3%, the highest since 1988 ([SBS](https://www.sbs.com.au/news/live-blog/israel-election-2026-live-updates/7z47797ge)). Preliminary results are due today, with official results on 4 November ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/27/exit-polls-following-israeli-elections-indicate-no-clear-winner)).
cards.why_it_matters: The result will have a significant bearing on the likelihood of escalation in the war with Iran, the main driver of oil prices, according to the AFR.
cards.what_to_watch: The official count, and which leader President Herzog asks to try to form a government.

competing_views.view: "The exit polls indicate complete lack of trust in Netanyahu," and said he would act immediately to replace Netanyahu's government.
No post-poll statement found before our cutoff. On polling day he urged right-wing supporters to vote, calling a high Arab vote a "matter of life or death" for them (SBS, with AFP).

cards.headline: Iran keeps its conditions as regional talks continue; Gulf attacks reported
cards.takeaway: Diplomacy is continuing, but there are new attack claims in the Gulf and Saudi Arabia, and Iran has not changed its demands.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's issue covered the envoys' arrival in Tehran. New: Khamenei's response, the four countries agreeing to keep talking, a Houthi strike claim on Ras Tanura, and an Iranian claim of a tanker hitting mines.
cards.what_happened: After the talks, Iran's security chief met Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who stressed maintaining Iran's conditions for ending the war, according to state media. The conditions include ending the US blockade of Iranian ports and US oil sanctions ([Reuters via Al-Monitor](https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/10/iran-security-chief-meets-supreme-leader-after-talks-mecca-pact-countries)). President Trump said of the war: "It's going to end very soon" ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/us-iran-war-peace-talks-donald-trump-strait-hormuz-october-27)). Iranian state media said the four countries agreed to continue talks ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/oil-eases-on-middle-east-diplomacy-hopes-saudi-attacks-keep-supply-worries-alive-4974185)). Yemen's Houthis said a missile hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm, and the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two missiles fired towards Riyadh ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/yemens-houthis-say-they-hit-saudi-ras-tanura-oil-refinery-with-missile-4976138)). Iran's navy said an unnamed tanker hit mines and caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz, and that the strait is "closed" to uncoordinated traffic ([Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-says-oil-tanker-catches-fire-after-hitting-naval-mine-east-of-strait-of-hormuz/4102560)). We found no independent confirmation.
cards.why_it_matters: Ras Tanura has capacity of 550,000 barrels a day, and it and Yanbu carry nearly all Saudi oil exports (Reuters). Saudi Arabia had contained a fire near the terminal, according to Bloomberg as cited by Reuters.
cards.what_to_watch: Saudi confirmation of any damage, the next round of talks, and Iran's planned legal action against Sinokor ships from 1 November (Fox News).

competing_views.who: Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's Supreme Leader (via CNBC)
competing_views.view: Said the "neither war nor peace" situation needs to end, while discussing Iran keeping control over Hormuz.
Said of the war: "It's going to end very soon."
